final_note: Cyclones need 26.5 degrees C surface temperature.

concepts.def: Low-pressure storm with sustained winds >118 km/h; called hurricane, typhoon or cyclone regionally.
Ring of intense thunderstorms around calm eye; strongest winds and rain.
Sea level rise from low pressure and wind; Hurricane Katrina surge reached 8.5 m.
Convergent plate boundary where oceanic crust dives beneath; sites of largest earthquakes.
Earthquake intensity from felt effects (I-XII); contrast with magnitude scales.
Saturated soil loses strength during shaking; collapsed buildings in Christchurch 2011.

walkthroughs.body_html: Requires SST > 26.5 degrees C, low wind shear, latitude > 5 degrees for Coriolis. Hurricane Katrina (2005) Cat 5 with 280 km/h winds. Storm surge 8.5 m. 1800 deaths, $125 billion damage; failed levees flooded 80 percent of New Orleans.

Sumatra 2004 Mw 9.1 quake displaced 1500 km of seafloor; tsunami killed 230000. Tohoku 2011 Mw 9.0 generated 40 m run-up at Miyako; Fukushima Daiichi reactor meltdowns followed. Subduction zones produce 90 percent of largest quakes.

Typhoon Haiyan 2013 (Cat 5, 315 km/h gusts) killed 6300 in Philippines with 7 m surge at Tacloban. Christchurch 2011 (Mw 6.3 shallow) killed 185 with widespread liquefaction. Both showed how secondary impacts (surge, liquefaction) dominate damage.
